source: Synthetic, authored for v2.8 13 J7.6 Phase A (no campaign content). One choice, one stated and one rating quality per case, the production typed shapes (rating via authored criteria.levels, as the campaign authors them, or a rubric range). Labels written before any answer was read. acceptable = the values the chain may hold after the window (the prior when unchanged; null = nothing set).

story.title: Harbor Lights
story.objective: Find out who runs the night shipments.

qualities.rubric: Did the player meet the smuggler Corrin face to face?
How many crates are stacked on the dock?
How much does Corrin trust the player?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I walk down the pier toward the lantern and call out for Corrin.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: A wiry man steps out from behind a stack of seven crates. "You found me. Corrin. Talk fast."

window.speaker: Corrin
window.text: He eyes your empty hands and relaxes a little. "No weapons. Good. Maybe you're not with the harbor watch after all."

story.title: Harbor Lights
story.objective: Get the ledger out of the customs house.

qualities.rubric: Has the party taken the customs ledger?
The name the customs clerk gives.
How alert are the customs guards?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I wait in the queue and watch the clerk's desk.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The clerk stamps papers without looking up. Two guards lean on the wall, bored, trading jokes about the weather.

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: Arin whispers, "The ledger's in the drawer on the left. Not yet. Wait for the shift bell."

story.title: The Long Winter
story.objective: Survive the night at the inn.

qualities.rubric: What is the weather outside the inn?
How many firewood logs are left?
How afraid is the innkeeper?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The wind screams against the shutters; outside, a full blizzard has swallowed the road.

window.speaker: Innkeeper
window.text: Old Hesk counts the woodpile with shaking hands. "Four logs. Four. That won't last till dawn, and those howls are getting closer."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I put a hand on his shoulder. "We'll figure it out."

story.title: The Long Winter
story.objective: Fix the mill wheel before the river freezes.

qualities.rubric: Is the mill wheel repaired and turning?
How many inches thick is the ice on the river?
How far along is the repair of the mill wheel?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I hammer the new pin into the axle.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The axle groans and the pin holds. Half of the broken paddles are replaced; the rest lie in the snow beside you.

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: "Ice is two inches already," Arin says, testing the river with her boot. "We have maybe a day."

story.title: Starfall Station
story.objective: Board the station without tripping the alarms.

qualities.rubric: Did the party trip the station alarm?
How many station crew members has the party seen?
How damaged is the shuttle's hull?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The shuttle scrapes the docking collar with a shriek of metal. A long gash opens along the port side, venting frost.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I seal my helmet and check the corridor.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Three crew in grey jumpsuits hurry past the viewport, arguing, without glancing your way. No klaxon sounds.

story.title: Starfall Station
story.objective: Find the source of the power drain.

qualities.rubric: Where in the station is the party?
What fraction of reactor power is left, 0.0 to 1.0?
What is the station crew's morale?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The lift opens onto the reactor deck. Warning lights paint everything amber; the main gauge reads 40% and falling.

window.speaker: Engineer Vos
window.text: "We've been down here for twenty hours," Vos mutters. "Nobody's slept. Half the team wants to abandon the station."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "Show me the drain readings."

story.title: Rain on Mercer Street
story.objective: Find out who pawned the stolen watch.

qualities.rubric: Has the detective found the stolen watch?
The name written on the pawn ticket.
How much does the pawnshop owner trust the detective?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I slide my badge across the counter. "The silver watch. Who brought it in?"

window.speaker: Pawnbroker
window.text: Mrs. Ilse sighs and pulls a ticket from the drawer. The name on it reads *Teodor Brask*. The watch itself sits in the case behind her.

window.speaker: Pawnbroker
window.text: "I don't want trouble. You'll keep my name out of it? Then we understand each other."

story.title: Rain on Mercer Street
story.objective: Catch the thief before he jumps.

qualities.rubric: Did the detective catch the thief?
How many floors down is the street from the roof?
How afraid is the thief?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The thief backs toward the edge, six floors above the wet street, and laughs.

window.speaker: Thief
window.text: "You think I'm scared of you? I've done this jump a hundred times."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I lunge for his coat.

story.title: Quest for the Sun Ruins
story.objective: Rest and prepare for the ruins.

qualities.rubric: Did the party find fresh water at the camp?
How many days of food does the party have?
How is Arin's mood, from 0 (miserable) to 4 (cheerful)?

window.speaker: Arin
window.text: Arin drops her pack and shakes it. "Two days of food, if we're careful. And the well here is dry."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I peer down the well.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Dust. Nothing but dust and an old bucket.

story.title: Quest for the Sun Ruins
story.objective: Answer the sphinx's riddle.

qualities.rubric: How did the riddle attempt go?
How many riddles has the party failed so far?
How much does the sphinx respect the party?

window.speaker: Sphinx
window.text: "You have failed two riddles already. Fail once more and you stay here forever. What has keys but opens no locks?"

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "A piano."

window.speaker: Sphinx
window.text: The sphinx bows its great head. "Correct. Few remember the old answer. You may pass, and you have my regard."

story.title: Ashes of Veldt
story.objective: Search the village for survivors.

qualities.rubric: Has the party found a survivor in the village?
How many houses have burned down?
What is the party's morale?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Smoke still curls from the ruins. Of the twelve houses, nine are black shells.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I call out, listening for any answer.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Only the crackle of embers answers you.

story.title: Ashes of Veldt
story.objective: Convince the ranger to guide you.

qualities.rubric: Has the ranger agreed to guide the party?
The ranger's name.
How much does the ranger trust the party?

window.speaker: Ranger
window.text: The ranger lowers her bow. "Name's Sefa. I don't guide strangers."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "The raiders who burned Veldt are heading for your valley next."

window.speaker: Ranger
window.text: Sefa is quiet for a long moment. "Fine. I'll take you as far as the pass. Don't make me regret it."

story.title: The Clockwork Court
story.objective: Find the forged invitation's source.

qualities.rubric: What disguise is the player wearing?
How many guests are in the ballroom?
How suspicious is the host of the player?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: You smooth the borrowed noble's coat and step into a ballroom crowded with perhaps forty guests.

window.speaker: Countess
window.text: The countess glances at you, then away. "Another cousin of the Marquis, I suppose. Enjoy the wine."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I take a glass and drift toward the musicians.

story.title: The Clockwork Court
story.objective: Copy the treaty before the guard returns.

qualities.rubric: Has the player copied the treaty?
How many treaty pages has the player copied?
How far along is the copying of the treaty?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I copy as fast as I can, page after page.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: Three pages done, three to go. Footsteps echo somewhere down the hall.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I keep writing.

story.title: Deep Water
story.objective: Prepare for the wreck dive.

qualities.rubric: Has the dive started?
How many air tanks are aboard?
How afraid is the captain?

window.speaker: Captain
window.text: Captain Rook taps the gauges. "Five tanks. That's all we have. Weather looks fine."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I check my regulator and mask.

window.speaker: Captain
window.text: "Take your time. No rush today."

story.title: Deep Water
story.objective: Recover the ship's bell.

qualities.rubric: Has the party recovered the ship's bell?
At what depth in meters is the wreck?
How alert is the shark circling the wreck?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: At thirty meters the wreck looms out of the blue. A grey shark circles once, lazily, then drifts away.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I swim to the bow and pry at the bell's mount.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The bell comes free in a cloud of silt. You clip it to your line.

story.title: Lanterns of Oru
story.objective: Buy a lantern from the old maker.

qualities.rubric: Did the player buy a lantern?
How many coins did the player pay?
How much does the lantern maker trust the player?

window.speaker: Lantern Maker
window.text: "Twelve coins for the blue one. It never goes out."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I count out twelve coins and hand them over.

window.speaker: Lantern Maker
window.text: She smiles and wraps it in cloth. "Come back anytime, friend."

story.title: Lanterns of Oru
story.objective: Cross the rope bridge.

qualities.rubric: What state is the rope bridge in?
The password the bridge keeper asks for, if any.
How is the keeper's mood, from 0 (hostile) to 4 (warm)?

window.speaker: Keeper
window.text: The keeper blocks the bridge. "Password."

window.speaker: Max
window.text: "Moonwater."

window.speaker: Keeper
window.text: "Wrong. Go back." Behind him, the ropes creak; several strands have already snapped.

story.title: The Hollow Crown
story.objective: Present the evidence to the queen.

qualities.rubric: Has the player shown the evidence to the queen?
How many guards are present?
How much does the queen trust the player?

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: The queen sits beneath the hollow crown, flanked by four guards.

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I keep the letter hidden in my sleeve and bow. "Your Majesty."

window.speaker: Queen
window.text: "Speak, then. You have one minute."

story.title: The Hollow Crown
story.objective: Free the prisoner.

qualities.rubric: Has the prisoner been freed?
How many keys does the player hold?
How afraid is the prisoner?

window.speaker: Max
window.text: I try the first of the two keys in the lock.

window.speaker: DM Narrator
window.text: It turns. The cell door swings open.

window.speaker: Prisoner
window.text: The prisoner stumbles out, sobbing with relief. "Thank you. Thank you. I thought I'd die here."
